title: Direct-image comparison
statement:
Fix a discrete commutative ring $\Lambda$, using its constant sheaves as coefficients. Let $g\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Base change of site objects gives
the commutative square of topoi

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X_{\Proet}&\xrightarrow{\ \nu_X\ }&X_{\Et}\\
{\scriptstyle g_{\Proet}}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle g_{\Et}}\\
Y_{\Proet}&\xrightarrow{\ \nu_Y\ }&Y_{\Et}
\end{array}
$$

and an isomorphism $g_{\Proet}^*\nu_Y^*\simeq\nu_X^*g_{\Et}^*$ of functors
$\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$, compatible with composition;
since all four functors are exact, it is also an isomorphism of functors
$D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$.

If $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the canonical natural
transformation of functors $D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to D^+(Y_{\Proet},\Lambda)$

$$
\nu_Y^*Rg_{\Et,*}K\longrightarrow Rg_{\Proet,*}\nu_X^*K
$$

is an isomorphism for $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. In particular, direct image of
a bounded-below classical pro-étale complex is classical. The isomorphism is
compatible with units, counits and composition.

proof.text: Apply inverseImageComparisonCoherence to obtain the identity and arbitrary-composition equations for the specified inverse-image square.

Synthesize exactness of all four inverse-image functors from their existing instances. The displayed unbounded transformation is the hom of an explicitly constructed natural isomorphism, so its invertibility is an existing instance.

Apply isIso_comparisonDirectImagePlus to the same canonical derived base-change transformation. Its unused finiteness hypothesis has been removed without changing its existing proof. Apply comparisonDirectImagePlus_id and comparisonDirectImagePlus_comp for the specified derived direct-image identity and arbitrary-composition equations.

Apply directImageMateCompatibility for the specified derived unit and counit equations. The unchanged real pullback comparison is defined in its new module, publicly reexported by the assigned module.

Apply classicalDirectImagePreservation to the bounded-below intrinsic classical complex, installing the supplied quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses as local instances. This is the classical-derived-equivalence route of the unit.
